member.summary: The maximum number of pixels (width × height) the decoder will accept before throwing. Guards against maliciously large dimensions causing excessive allocation. Defaults to 500 million.

member.name: P:JpegSharp.Api.JpegDecoderOptions.MaxDecodedBytes
member.summary: The maximum estimated PEAK decode allocation, in bytes, the decoder will accept before throwing. Unlike , this bounds actual memory: it accounts for the component sample planes (2 bytes/sample at 12-bit precision, 1 byte at 8-bit), the per-component coefficient buffers a progressive (SOF2) decode additionally allocates, the full-size chroma-upsampling scratch plane each subsampled component allocates during assembly, and the final output image buffer. A pixel count alone does not bound memory, since a multi-component, 12-bit, and/or progressive image consumes far more bytes per pixel than a single-component 8-bit baseline image. Enforced ALONGSIDE (whichever limit trips first), and independently of the internal int-overflow guards. Defaults to 1 GiB (1,073,741,824 bytes).

member.name: P:JpegSharp.Api.JpegDecoderOptions.StrictRestartMarkers
member.summary: Controls how restart markers (RST0–RST7) are validated at restart-interval boundaries. When false (the default), a missing or out-of-sequence restart marker is handled leniently: the decoder resyncs, resets its DC predictors and continues, matching its general tolerance of truncated or corrupt entropy data. When true, a missing or misordered restart marker throws .

member.name: T:JpegSharp.Transforms.Dct
member.summary: Reference 8x8 two-dimensional Discrete Cosine Transform (type II) and its inverse, implemented in the orthonormal (energy-preserving) formulation used by JPEG.

remarks.para: The transform is separable: a 2D DCT of an 8x8 block equals A · f · Aᵀ where A is the orthonormal 1D DCT basis matrix. The implementation therefore applies a 1D transform to the rows and then to the columns, giving O(n³) work per block on a tiny fixed 8x8 grid.

This is the numerically exact reference transform used to validate the faster integer/AAN fixed-point paths. Because the basis is orthonormal, and are exact inverses (to floating-point tolerance) and the DC coefficient of a flat block equals eight times the sample value.

member.summary: Fixed-point (integer) inverse 8x8 DCT modelled on libjpeg-turbo's "islow" transform (jidctint.c). Uses 13-bit constants with a two-pass Loeffler-style factorization: the column pass keeps 2 guard bits () and the row pass performs the final descale.
